guarantees.text: It provides `enableScope`, `disableScope` and `toggleScope` to control scopes by name, and `activeScopes` to read the scopes that are currently enabled.
Wrapping the app in `HotkeysProvider` enables the wildcard scope "*" by default.
When `initiallyActiveScopes` is set, the wildcard scope "*" is not active unless it is in the array, so ["scopeA", "*"] activates both.
When several keys are given, `isHotkeyPressed` returns `true` only if all of them are pressed down, and `false` otherwise.
The `key` argument may be a single keycode such as "a", a delimited string such as "shift,a", or an array such as ["shift", "a"].
The `delimiter` used to split multiple keys from a single string is "," by default.

The `options` defaults are `enabled` true, `enableOnFormTags` false, `enableOnContentEditable` false, `splitKey` "+", `delimiter` ",", `scopes` "*", `keydown` true, `preventDefault` false, `ignoreModifiers` false, `useKey` false, `sequenceTimeoutMs` 1000 and `sequenceSplitKey` ">".
Setting `keyup` to `true` without setting `keydown` listens to `keyup` only; to listen to both, `keydown` and `keyup` must both be `true`.
With the default `delimiter` ",", the keys "ctrl+a, shift+b" listen for either combination, and with the default `splitKey` "+", "shift+a" fires when Shift and A are pressed together.
With the keys "g>h>i" the user must press g, then h, then i in order, and the sequence resets if the next key is not pressed within `sequenceTimeoutMs`, which is 1000 milliseconds by default.
The `keys` argument is case-insensitive: "CTRL+S", "Ctrl+s" and "ctrl+S" all listen for the `ctrl` and `s` keys, and an uppercase letter is treated as lowercase.
The modifiers are "shift", "alt", "ctrl", "meta" and "mod", where "mod" triggers when either `ctrl` or `meta` is pressed, and "alt" and "option" are treated as identical.
When `enabled` is the boolean `false` the event listeners are removed, and when `enabled` is a function that returns `false` the listeners stay attached but the callback is skipped.
It returns a React ref callback; when it is attached to an element, the hotkey fires only when that element or one of its children has focus.

units.returns: readonly [Set<string>, { readonly start: () => void; readonly stop: () => void; readonly resetKeys: () => void; readonly isRecording: boolean; }]

guarantees.text: By default `useKey` is `false` and the hook records key codes, so pressing Shift+1 records "shift+1".
With `useKey` set to `true` the hook records the produced character, so pressing Shift+1 on a US layout records "!".
The `blacklist` is empty by default, and keys named in it, such as "tab" and "enter", are not added to the recorded keys and keep their default behavior.
The first returned value is a `Set` of strings in which each recorded key appears only once.
The second returned value has `start`, `stop`, `resetKeys` and `isRecording`, where `isRecording` is `true` while recording is active and `false` otherwise.
Calling `resetKeys` clears the recorded keys.
